questions.stem: Which multiplication has the same answer as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3?
questions.stemText: Which multiplication has the same answer as 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 + 3 ?
questions.explain: Count the 3s: there are 5 of them, so this is 5 groups of 3, which is 5 × 3 = 15. Counting one group too few gives 4 × 3, which is 3 too little, and multiplying the wrong pair gives 3 × 3 or 4 × 5. Multiplication is a short way of writing the same number added over and over - that is the whole idea, and it is why the times tables are worth knowing by heart.

questions.stem: Priya works out 1205 + 3228 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.stemText: Priya works out 1205 + 3228 in columns. One column makes 13, so she writes 3 in that column and a small 1 above the column on its left. How much is that small 1 worth?
questions.explain: The column that makes 13 is the ones column: 5 + 8 = 13, and no other column reaches ten. 13 ones is 1 ten and 3 ones, so the 3 stays in the ones column - worth 3 - and the small 1 goes above the tens column - worth 10. The small 1 is worth 10. A mark is worth the column it is written in, not the digit it looks like: that is what regrouping means, ten of something small becoming one of the next size up. Every wrong answer here is one of the two slips - the right digit read in the wrong column, or the wrong digit read in the right one.

questions.stem: Priya has four digit cards: 0, 1, 3, 8. She uses each card once to make a 4-digit number. What is the smallest odd number she can make?
questions.stemText: Priya has four digit cards: 0 , 1 , 3 , 8 . She uses each card once to make a 4-digit number. What is the smallest odd number she can make?
questions.explain: An odd number ends in 1, 3, 5, 7 or 9, so the ones card must be 1 or 3. Try each one in the ones place, and each time make the smallest number you can from the other three cards. The 0 cannot go first: a number that starts with 0 is not a 4-digit number. With 1 last: 3081. With 3 last: 1083. The smallest of these is 1083. (1038 is smaller, but it is even, so it does not count.)

Now add up the digits of each one: 9 + 5 + 5 + 0 = 19; 9 + 6 + 5 + 1 = 21; 9 + 7 + 5 + 2 = 23; 9 + 8 + 5 + 3 = 25; 9 + 9 + 5 + 4 = 27. Only 9954 has digits that add up to 27.

questions.explain: Buying 4 packets of ang ku kueh one by one costs 4 × $2 = $8, but 4 for $7 is cheaper, so buy as many bundles as you can. 13 ÷ 4 = 3 remainder 1, so 3 bundles cost 3 × $7 = $21. The 1 packet of ang ku kueh left over cost 1 × $2 = $2 (cheaper than one more bundle at $7). Total: $21 + $2 = $23. Buying all 13 one by one would cost $26.

questions.stem: A rectangular banner is 15 cm long and 8 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 3 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 4 cm of edge before the notch and 7 cm after it, and the banner is still 5 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.stemText: A rectangular banner is 15 cm long and 8 cm wide. A notch 4 cm wide and 3 cm deep is cut out of the middle of one long side, so the notch does not reach either end. Along that side there is 4 cm of edge before the notch and 7 cm after it, and the banner is still 5 cm wide behind the notch. Every corner is a right angle. What is the perimeter of the banner now?
questions.explain: Walk the eight sides: 4 + 3 + 4 + 3 + 7 + 8 + 15 + 8 = 52 cm. Careful: this notch is in the middle of a side, not at a corner. The 4 cm taken out of the top edge is replaced by the 4 cm along the bottom of the notch, so that part of the walk is unchanged. But the two sides of the notch, 3 cm down and 3 cm back up, are brand new. Perimeter = 2 × (15 + 8) + 2 × 3 = 52 cm. A corner cut leaves the perimeter alone; a middle notch makes it longer.
